Acoma, "City of the Sky," perched on a 400 foot high mesa, casts its
shadow on the desert floor.
TRAVEL BY AIR
Transcontinental & Western Air, Inc.,
"The Lindbergh
Line " flies the Shortest Route from Coast to Coast through the
great mid-transcontinental belt of cities and closely parallels
through the West one of the oldest known trade channels in
America — The Santa Fe Trail. The Lindbergh Line, associated
with the Pennsylvania Railroad, was the pioneer in establishing
the first transcontinental air passenger service and also was the
Cific Corator of multi-motored passenger equipment on the Pa-
Attuned to the needs of the modern American who travels
for business or pleasure, the passenger transport airplanes of
TWA provide a service which is at once deluxe and common-
place.
Deluxe because of the comfort, convenience and pleasure
they afford; commonplace to thousands of travelers who have
adopted the airplane as a routine, every-day necessity.
TWA is
proud of its six year record and its important contribution to
America's supremacy in air transportation. It is the main arterv
of travel in this modern era where conservation of time and
energy are requisite to success and contentment.
TWA renders complete air transport service between
score of cities directly on its route and through connections with
other air, rail and bus lines makes available to you swift, depend-
able service to every important city and town in the United
States.
TWA offers a route rich in scenic beauty. Vistas of moun-
tain and valley.
desert and
canyon: the ruins of prehistoric
cities; sheer-walled mesas and rocky cliffs freakishly carved by
wind and weather: the Petrified Forest and The Painted Desert:
picturesque Indian villages, the atmosphere of Old Spain in
America - all this and much more is to be seen while flying the
Shortest Route from Coast to Coast over TWA.
Appetizing luncheons served aloft.
TRANSCONTINENTAL & WESTERN AIR
Offers You...
An economical, comfortable means of travel in the finest,
most modern, flying equipment.
A corps of veteran pilots with years of flying experience.
Planes equipped with radio-telephones and directional
beacon service.
Complete weather reports over each 24-hour period.
Lighted and improved airways and airports over its entire
system.
Luncheons served aloft, included in the fare.
Competent personnel with years of transportation experi-
ence.
Strict enforcerent of the most rigid maintenance stand-
ards.
Modern and completely equipped passenger terminals.
Every office of the Pennsylvania Railroad, Postal Tele-
graph and Western
Union, Greyhound Bus; also
travel bureaus, hotel porters, and TWA offices in a
score of cities, as sources of information and tickets,
... and...

SHIP BY GENERAL AIR EXPRESS
As an outgrowth of its pioneering activity in the air ship-
ing field, TWA has perfected a system for the fastest possible
method of shipping merchandise which is meeting with broad
public acceptance.
Merchants, manufacturers, and shippers generally have
found air express offers a distinct advantage for making over-
night delivery of merchandise with no loss of business time be
tween New York, Chicago, St. Louis,
Kansas City and other
midwest cities, also from coast to coast in twenty-three hours.
Through a new interline arrangement with six other air-
lines, all points on the TWA system are now linked with 138
cities in the United States with connections to Canada. Mexico,
and South America. This new service known as General Air Ex-
press,
"the interline system"
permits the free exchange of mer
chandise between all sections of the country on through waybills
and under standard shipping conditions. Through rates, including
store-door pickup and delivery service by
Postal Telegraph are
published in a joint tariff which mav be obtained from any TWA
representative or from any Postal Telegraph office.
Progressive sales managers are finding in air express new
opportunities to reach new markets to cut down inventories and
to speed up
the turnover of merchandise. It affords
an ideal
service for the distribution of samples,
shipments which cannot
afford to lose days in transit, the rapid transmission of important
machinery parts and for the quick replacement of stocks in va-
rious sections of the country at surprisingly low rates.
Cargo in-
surance at low rates is available to all shippers and individual
packages weighing as much as 200 pounds will be accepted to
all points.
